body: Yes, TTLs for v3 leases use a relative clock, they don't rely on system time.
I used the etcd 3.0.12 version, but I found when the system time changes manually, the expire time will be changed also. shall I do some configuration to have this relative clock?
@nenzhang oh, I see your point. Leases use time.Now() to compute the expiry deadline and the system clock could jump around (probably broken for day light savings time?). Marking as a bug. Thanks!
@heyitsanthony We probably can convert it to logical clock somehow. Do you think this is something we should fix soon?
Definitely should have a fix before November 6th...
added into the most recent milestone.

Hi
Ok, good to hear this. 
if you can fix this as earlier as possible, then it is will be really good news to us.

Even with system real time, I assume it should use the master system time. 
In our case, the NTP was set to different NTP server accidentally. Whenever we set TTL key on local non master node, the key was deleted.  It turns out the expiring time is from local node, and it already behind master current time.
@heyitsanthony @xiang90  The Go issue got delayed to Go 1.9, which is another 6+ months.

issue.title: Use monotonic time in lease

repository.name: etcd
repository.description: Distributed reliable key-value store for the most critical data of a distributed system

issue.body:
lease uses monotimer to calculate its expiration. In this way, changing system time won't affect in lease expiration.

FIX #6700
